source: Feng X J, Zhang J T, Lin H, Gillis K A, Moldover M R (2015). Determination of the Boltzmann Constant Using the Differential - Cylindrical Procedure. arXiv:1501.02519
paper_txt_rule_check: pdftotext -layout demo/paper.pdf - is byte-identical to demo/paper.txt (41,121 bytes, sha256 1294dc34b73f9b2a...), checked 2026-11-02
cut_rule: first cut_lines lines of the stripped extraction, then .strip(); the cut is a paragraph boundary (build_feng2015.paragraph_ends)

claude_input_tokens.method: cut 979 is NOT measured. Estimate = calibration at cut 813 (overhead-corrected) + Claude-per-proxy-token on Feng, see recut_from_calibration.py and MANIFEST.md
claude_input_tokens.cli_version_note: arm0/armB anchors include CLI overhead (~11.6k tokens) that may differ by CLI version; the block difference cancels it, absolute counts do not. Compare armX only against counts taken under the same CLI version.

calibration.status: NOT SAMPLES. Excluded from every denominator before the calls were made; transcripts in demo/transcripts/calibration/, no arms/*/k*.py written
calibration.script: demo/controls/calibrate.py --arm armB --arm armX (ClaudeCliBackend(timeout=1800), the flags generate.py uses)
calibration.turn1_source: per-request usage in the CLI session logs (~/.claude/projects/-tmp-gen-clean-*/<session_id>.jsonl); the --output-format json usage sums all turns

extra_overhead_in_armX_call.what: the armX session loaded the account's claude.ai MCP connectors (Claude Docs, Gmail, ...) and the armB session did not: +5,574 chars in the environment block (MCP tool names, MCP server instructions) and 3 MCP tool definitions (1,930 chars). System prompt and tool-schema shape hash identical otherwise.
extra_overhead_in_armX_call.r_source: Claude/proxy fitted on the armB call's own non-paper message text (reminders + environment block + task): (26464 - 8066 cached prefix - 12766 block) / proxy count; upper bound, message framing is folded in. Paper block gives 1.473 / 1.480.

calibration.verdict: cut 813 is NOT within +-0.5 % (about -6 % after removing the extra overhead; -1.9 % to -6.6 % for r in [1.0, 1.48]). Re-cut once, to 979 (recut_from_calibration.py). No second calibration call made.
